item.title: MSCI gets set to remove Indonesia from global indexes, sparks market slide to six-year low
item.description: Indonesia's stock market is no longer worthy of "emerging market" status, according to MSCI, and the index provider said it intends to cut it from a suite of products tracked by global investors, a major setback that sent money fleeing.
item.dc:creator: Reuters
item.content:encoded: Indonesia's stock market is no longer worthy of "emerging market" status, according to MSCI, and the index provider said it intends to cut it from a suite of products tracked by global investors, a major setback that sent money fleeing. In a surprise move, MSCI said on Friday it would put Indonesia on a path to "standalone" status, which was worse than previously flagged, and extended its review of the market by seven months to June 2027. Jakarta stocks (.JKSE) , already the world's worst performers this year, plunged 10% to a six-year low in early trading, while the rupiah slid 0.6% to 18,000 per US dollar, its weakest level since August. Indonesian equities have struggled since January when MSCI froze Indonesia in its indexes and threatened a downgrade to "frontier" status because of opacity in ownership and trading behaviour. On Friday, MSCI said reforms to address those problems have not made sufficient progress and that even a downgrade to frontier wouldn't reflect the severity of issues. Instead, it proposed to downgrade Indonesia to "standalone" status, which would exclude Indonesian stocks from global indexes tracked by billions of dollars in passive investment, forcing funds that follow or are ranked against the indexes to sell. "Significant concerns remain around market dysfunction," MSCI said. "Accordingly, MSCI considers Indonesia's continued classification as an emerging market no longer appropriate," it said. "Feedback from market participants suggests that a reclassification to frontier markets would not properly recognize the depth of the market problems." The Indonesia Stock Exchange said it has taken concrete steps to enhance transparency and integrity in the country's capital market, and CEO Jeffrey Hendrik said in a statement he would request further clarification on the basis for the announcement. Coming a month ahead of a scheduled review, MSCI's statement stunned investors and Jakarta officials, with the chief of Indonesia's financial regulator Friderica Widyasari Dewi saying she did not expect the announcement following a meeting this week. Finance minister Suahasil Nazara, who chairs the country's financial stability board, did not immediately reply to a request for comment on the MSCI announcement. Angus Mackintosh, an ASEAN specialist at Aletheia Capital in Singapore, said the move does not reflect the health of the vast majority of listed companies or indeed the Indonesian economy, and "grouping Indonesia with Lebanon, Palestine, and Argentina does not make sense." "This is a wake-up call for Indonesia," he said. DOWNGRADE PLANNED FOR MID-2027 MSCI's move seemed heavy-handed given the steps Indonesia has taken to [USN:L6N42W0D2 TEXT:"address issues"] around market transparency and increase the free-float requirement for listed firms, Mackintosh said. The main problem, he said, is Indonesia's "failure to sanction those obviously involved in stock manipulation". MSCI said it will run a consultation with market participants for a downgrade to "standalone" status until April 2027 and then proceed with reclassification unless it finds clear evidence of improvement in market governance and function. Standalone markets are not included in MSCI's emerging or frontier index products, which are tracked by passive funds and treated as performance benchmarks for other fund managers. MSCI says reclassification to standalone status may occur in the case of severe deterioration in market accessibility or size and liquidity, with the most recent example being Argentina. Gary Tan, portfolio manager at Allspring Global Investments, Singapore, called the move a surprise, noting the prospect of a standalone status could encourage index-linked investors to further de-risk. "But for Indonesia, in our view, the bigger concern is less the direct impact on equities and more the potential pressure on the currency from foreign outflows." Indonesia has faced a series of setbacks this year, with [USN:L4N3Z114D TEXT:"Moody's"] and [USN:L1N3ZS06T TEXT:"Fitch"] cutting their sovereign rating outlooks to negative, citing reduced policymaking credibility. The benchmark Jakarta stock index (.JKSE) has fallen more than 30% this year, making it the worst-performing equity market in the world, with net selling by foreign investors at $4.7 billion worth of shares.

FAST

ORLANDO, Florida, Oct 15 : The AI equity rout accelerated significantly in Asia on Thursday on growing fears about the murky, circular financing powering the intelligence revolution's buildout, although its force evaporated in European and US trading hours. Still, safe-haven inflows meant US Treasuries had one of their best days in months, despite a surprisingly strong rise in US producer inflation. Today's Key Reads • CoreWeave's slump spotlights growing burden of debt behind AI boom • AI credit worries send default insurance to record high

• AI investment boom may be papering over US economic cracks: Mike Dolan • US producer prices post largest gain in 4-1/2 years; expensive gasoline boosts retail sales • Warsh's quest for quiet Fed gets vocal pushback • Today's Key Market Moves STOCKS: Asia in the red, South Korea -7.5 per cent to 6-month low, Japan -5 per cent. UK +1 per cent to 7-week high. Nasdaq +0.1 per cent, S&P 500 +0.3 per cent, Dow +1 per cent.SECTORS/SHARES: Eight sectors on the S&P 500 rise, three fall. Tech -0.5 per cent, energy -1.5 per cent, healthcare +2 per cent. CoreWeave +6.5 per cent, Nike +5 per cent. Hewlett Packard, Dell -7 per cent.FX: Dollar slides, biggest fall in six weeks. Biggest gainer is Swiss franc, +1 per cent; biggest decliner is Brazilian real, -1.5 per cent.BONDS: Bund yield -11 bps to 3.35 per cent, lowest in over a month. US 10-year yield -10 bps to 5.08 per cent, curve flattens. CoreWeave and other AI corporate bonds rise.COMMODITIES/METALS: Oil mixed — Brent flat, WTI +3 per cent. Gold +1 per cent, silver +3 per cent. Today's Talking Points: Funny money The global AI trade has hit some major turbulence. South Korea's KOSPI, a top 10 global index, has lost 20 per cent of its value in barely a week, and on Thursday Japan's Nikkei slid 5 per cent. CoreWeave 2032 bonds issued just four months ago fell below 80 cents in the dollar, typically considered distressed debt levels, and the cost of insuring against major US AI firms defaulting has soared to record levels. As ever, credit markets are likely to lead equities, and the risk of a self-fulfilling doom loop cannot be ignored — selling in certain names casts a shadow over healthier credits, and downgrades and loss of investment-grade ratings could force further selling. All while cash has been spent, and capex is increasingly being financed by debt, private credit and off-balance-sheet borrowing. We're not at crisis point yet — look at the rebound in US stocks and bonds today — but vigilance is required. Bonds be bonds Incoming data shows US producer price inflation is running hotter than expected, like CPI the day before, WTI crude spikes another 3 per cent, and Treasuries rally. Sounds counterintuitive, especially given how heavily fixed income markets have traded in recent weeks, but it shows that the demise of Treasuries' safe-haven appeal has been greatly exaggerated. Thursday was one of the best days of the year for Treasuries, especially for maturities of 10 years and beyond. The question is whether this is a knee-jerk move, or will continued volatility in equities and weakness in AI-related corporate debt remind investors that the best place to hedge, diversify and protect their capital is the traditional "risk-free" asset? Guaranteed nominal yields of over 5 per cent appear to be tempting. Rotation, rotation, rotation Wall Street's resilience on Thursday was pretty remarkable, given the ferocity of the tech selloff in Asia and weight of negative sentiment at the session open. Chip stocks fell for a seventh day, their longest losing streak in four years, but the Nasdaq edged higher and, more impressively, the Dow rose 1 per cent to its highest in a month. As the US earnings season kicks into gear, the focus will be on tech. The bar of expectations is high, and if it is not hurdled, investors may decide to ramp up the rotation into other sectors. How long do rotations out of tech last? According to Deutsche Bank, since mid-2024 the average length of rotation is 67 days and the median is 59 days. In terms of tech drawdowns over these periods, the average is 16.6 per cent and the median is 14.6 per cent. What could move markets tomorrow? • IMF/World Bank meetings in Bangkok, Fed Chair Kevin Warsh, ECB President Christine Lagarde, and BoE Governor Andrew Bailey among several officials speaking • Euro zone trade (August) • Euro zone inflation (September, final) • US import prices (September) • US industrial production (September) Want to receive Trading Day in your inbox every weekday morning? They do not reflect the views of Reuters News, which, under the Trust Principles, is committed to integrity, independence, and freedom from bias.

item.title: Investors temper Anthropic IPO valuation expectations over revenue growth slowdown, sources say
item.description: Some current Anthropic investors and prospective investors in its upcoming initial public offering are weighing a lower valuation for the AI company after its latest financial disclosures, four people familiar with the matter said, amid broader concerns over the ballooning cost of financing AI.
item.dc:creator: Milana Vinn, Anirban Sen
item.content:encoded: Some current Anthropic investors and prospective investors in its upcoming initial public offering are weighing a lower valuation for the AI company after its latest financial disclosures, four people familiar with the matter said, amid broader concerns over the ballooning cost of financing AI. Some investors who attended [USN:L6N4601AA TEXT:"Anthropic's investor day"] on Wednesday in San Francisco discussed a valuation of around $1.5 trillion, three of the people said, a significant step down from the roughly $2 trillion valuation that investors had previously expected for the November share sale. At Wednesday's meeting, Anthropic told prospective IPO investors that its third-quarter revenue jumped 45% to $16.8 billion from the previous quarter, and that it was profitable on an adjusted basis during the quarter. While those numbers assuaged some concerns about the massive costs of developing AI systems, some investors were disappointed by the slowing sequential growth rate in the latest quarter, as Anthropic's revenue more than doubled from the first quarter to $11.6 billion in the second quarter, the people added. They spoke on condition of anonymity because they are not authorized to speak publicly on the matter. Anthropic did not immediately respond to requests for comment. A cooler reception for Anthropic's IPO could weigh on the wider AI market, whose near-term prospects investors see as hinging largely on the share sale's success, followed by [USN:L6N45407M TEXT:"OpenAI's potential listing"] next year. BELLWETHER IPO The concerns from investors come as a tech selloff is roiling global financial markets and has hurt AI infrastructure companies, chipmakers and so-called neocloud providers that rent computing power for AI broadly. Shares and bonds of Nvidia (NVDA.O) -backed CoreWeave (CRWV.O) [USN:L4N46111C TEXT:" tumbled on Thursday"], reflecting growing investor concern about an AI buildout that is increasingly being financed with borrowed money. A disappointing share sale for Anthropic could further add to investor worries about the AI buildout. The IPO market has suffered [USN:L6N45H0SG TEXT:"some setbacks"] recently, after data center operator SB Energy decided to delay its listing last month, while nuclear technology company Holtec Nuclear [USN:L4N4581N0 TEXT:"pulled its plans to go public"]. During Wednesday's meeting at Anthropic's headquarters in San Francisco, attendees, mostly the company's most prominent investors, met with CEO Dario Amodei and finance chief Krishna Rao. The Information earlier reported that investors were considering a lower valuation. Founded in 2021 by former OpenAI executives including Amodei and his sister Daniela Amodei, who is now Anthropic's president, Anthropic has emerged as one of the leading generative AI developers with its Claude family of models. The company's rapid growth has been underpinned by Alphabet's (GOOGL.O) Google and Amazon (AMZN.O) , which are simultaneously investors, suppliers of computing power and important distribution partners, as well as AI competitors. Last year, Anthropic's revenue surged twelvefold to nearly $4.6 billion, even as the company lost more than $8 billion on an operating basis, excluding writedowns of various liabilities mostly tied to previous fundraising, Reuters [USN:L4N4500J8 TEXT:"reported "]last month. In its IPO prospectus seen exclusively by Reuters in September, Anthropic laid out a vision that AI will transform the global economy more profoundly than industrialization, electricity and the internet, even as it reported a loss of $42 billion in 2025 and projected more spending for the upcoming AI buildout. The company has committed to spending [USN:L1N45K0RM TEXT:"at least $518 billion"] over a decade for cloud services, computing and infrastructure.

item.title: ＮＹ外為市場＝ドル下落、ＡＩ関連企業への懸念が重し 10月利上げ観測後退
item.description: ［ニューヨーク １５日 ロイター］ - ニューヨーク外為市場では、ドルが円やユーロなどの主要通貨に対し下落した。連邦準備...
item.dc:creator: ロイター
item.content:encoded:
ＮＹ外為市場＝ドル下落、ＡＩ関連企業への懸念が重し　10月利上げ観測後退 5:53 配信

２０１１年１月撮影　REUTERS/Kacper Pempel

［ニューヨーク　１５日　ロイター］ - ニューヨーク外為市場では、ドルが円やユーロなどの主要通貨に対し下落した。連邦準備理事会（ＦＲＢ）当局者の慎重な発言を受け１０月の利上げ観測が後退しているほか、この日発表された堅調な物価・消費関連指標よりもＡＩ（人工知能）向けデータセンター関連企業を巡る懸念に市場の関心が集まったことがドルの重しになった。

この日発表の米経済指標では、９月の小売売上高が前月比０．８％増加。ガソリン価格の上昇を背景に予想を上回る伸びとなったが、ガソリン以外の支出は総じて緩やかで、自動車、ガソリン、建設資材、外食サービスを除くコア小売売上高は前月比０．１％増と、伸びは前月から鈍化した。

９月の卸売物価指数（ＰＰＩ、最終需要向け財・サービス）は前年比６．３％上昇。２０２２年１２月以来の大幅な伸びとなり、エネルギー関連以外にもインフレが広がっている可能性が改めて示された。

マネックスＵＳＡのトレーディング部門責任者、フアン・ペレス氏は「現在のインフレ率とその上昇ペースは持続不可能との見方から、ドルに弱気な相場観が広がっている」と指摘。「景気停滞を巡る懸念が市場心理に大きく影響する中、この４週間の大幅なドル高を受けて市場はドル売りに傾いている」と述べた。

前日に発表された９月の消費者物価指数（ＣＰＩ）は前年比は３．７％上昇と、伸びは前月の３．４％から加速。予想の３．６％も上回った。これを受け、当初はＦＲＢは追加利上げに動くとの見方が強まったものの、その後、ボウマンＦＲＢ副議長やサンフランシスコ地区連銀のデイリー総裁が判断材料を見極める時間的余裕があるとの認識を示したことで、利上げ観測は後退した。

ＣＭＥフェドウオッチによると、ＦＲＢが２７─２８日の会合で金利据え置きを決定する確率は７３％。１カ月前の５３％から上昇した。

ロンドンのＬＭＡＸグループで市場ストラテジストを務めるジョエル・クルーガー氏は、ＡＩ関連企業の多額の債務負担への懸念が再燃したことで安全資産とされる米国債に資金が流入していることに関連し、「国債利回りの上昇が続かず、ドル相場の上昇局面で売りが続く場合、インフレ関連の材料はおおむね市場に織り込まれたとの見方が強まる。その場合、リスク資産に有利な方向に市場のリスクバランスが傾く」と述べた。

市場ではＦＲＢの金融政策の行方を見極めようと、ウォーシュＦＲＢ議長が１６日にバンコクで開かれる国際通貨基金（ＩＭＦ）・世界銀行年次総会で行う講演が注目されている。

メシロー・カレンシー・マネジメントのシニア投資戦略担当者、ウト・シノハラ氏は「ＦＲＢはまもなく（ＦＯＭＣ前後に金融政策に関する発言を控える）ブラックアウト期間に入る上、ＦＯＭＣまでに重要な経済指標の発表は残されていない」とし、「このため、市場の方向性は引き続きロシア・ウクライナ情勢やイランを巡る地政学的な不透明感に加え、ＡＩを巡る動向に左右される可能性が高い」としている。

終盤の取引で主要通貨に対するドル指数は０．４５％安の１０１．９９。前日は１年６カ月ぶりの高値を付けていた。

ユーロは対ドルで０．５６％高の１．１２１８ドル。円は対ドルで０．１５％高の１５８．０８円。

item.title: TSE proíbe Meta de restringir conteúdo eleitoral e favorecer Lula ou Flávio com ferramenta de IA
item.description: O ministro Marco Aurélio Bellizze, do Tribunal Superior Eleitoral (TSE), proibiu nesta quinta-feira que a Meta restrinja sem justificativa o alcance da divulgação de conteúdos político-eleitorais relacionados às campanhas do presidente Luiz Inácio Lula da Silva (PT) e do senador Flávio Bolsonaro (PL) até o final do segundo turno.
item.dc:creator: Ricardo Brito
item.content:encoded: O ministro Marco Aurélio Bellizze, do Tribunal Superior Eleitoral (TSE), proibiu nesta quinta-feira que a Meta restrinja sem justificativa o alcance da divulgação de conteúdos político-eleitorais relacionados às campanhas do presidente Luiz Inácio Lula da Silva (PT) e do senador Flávio Bolsonaro (PL) até o final do segundo turno. Bellizze também determinou que a Meta AI, ferramenta de inteligência artificial da empresa que funciona como um Chatbot não favoreça qualquer das duas candidaturas na produção de conteúdos eleitorais. Em caso de descumprimento, segundo a decisão vista pela Reuters, poderá estabelecer multa diária de R$ 500 mil. Procurada na noite desta quinta-feira, a Meta -- companhia dona das redes sociais Instagram, WhatsApp e Facebook -- disse que não vai comentar. REUNIÃO Representantes da Meta disseram mais cedo nesta quinta ao TSE que estavam trabalhando no aperfeiçoamento de filtros da Meta AI, o assistente de inteligência artificial desenvolvido pela companhia, informou a corte eleitoral após reunião entre as partes. Segundo comunicado divulgado pelo TSE, o presidente e o vice-presidente do tribunal, Kassio Nunes Marques e André Mendonça, reuniram-se com representantes da Meta (META.O) "para debater as ferramentas utilizadas pela empresa que podem contribuir para o período eleitoral brasileiro". O encontro ocorreu um dia após a campanha à reeleição de Lula [USN:L1N46013H TEXT:"recorrer"] ao TSE e até a Organização dos Estados Americanos (OEA) acusando a big tech de usar inteligência artificial e algoritmos para favorecer Flávio Bolsonaro. O TSE disse, no comunicado desta quinta-feira, que a preocupação é promover uma “paridade de armas” entre os candidatos para que o eleitor possa escolher livremente. "Segundo a empresa (Meta), nesta semana, as duas campanhas foram impactadas pela geração de conteúdos de inteligência artificial considerados inadequados", disse o TSE em comunicado. Procurada, a Meta respondeu que no comunicado divulgado pelo TSE estão todas as informações disponíveis. Os ministros do TSE, conforme a nota, mencionaram também o tema do uso dos canais de WhatsApp para promover conteúdo eleitoral. "A Meta informou que, de acordo com a política da empresa, as mensagens enviadas nos canais não são criptografadas", disse a empresa, segundo o TSE. De acordo com o TSE, a Meta se comprometeu ainda a empenhar os esforços necessários para vedar eventuais impulsionamentos de conteúdos de propaganda eleitoral feitos com moeda estrangeira.

item.title: アンソロピック、外部評価機関ＭＥＴＲに社員並みアクセス ＡＩ安全性強化へ
item.description:
Aditya Soni
[１５日 ロイター] - 米人工知能（ＡＩ）開発企業のアンソロピックは１５日、ＡＩの安全性を...
item.dc:creator: ロイター
item.content:encoded:
アンソロピック、外部評価機関ＭＥＴＲに社員並みアクセス　ＡＩ安全性強化へ 5:36 配信

米カリフォルニア州サンフランシスコで開催されたDreamforce 2026テクノロジーサミットで９月撮影。REUTERS/Carlos Barria

Aditya Soni

[１５日 ロイター] - 米人工知能（ＡＩ）開発企業のアンソロピックは１５日、ＡＩの安全性を研究する非営利団体ＭＥＴＲに、自社システムへの社員レベルのアクセス権を付与したと明らかにした。ＡＩ新興企業ハギングフェイス など他の組織とも協議中という。ＡＩ各社は、技術開発のペースを遅らせることなく安全性を高める手段として、外部評価機関の活用を打ち出している。

アンソロピックはブログで、生物安全保障分野の非営利団体「セキュアバイオ」や、コンサルティング大手アクセンチュアのＡＩ事業部門ファカルティーも評価機関として起用していると説明した。

アンソロピックによると、ＭＥＴＲの職員６人には、同社のハードウエア、オフィススペースのほか、社内のリスク評価チームとほぼ同等の内部システムへのアクセス権が与えられる。ただし、顧客データ、法的機密情報、モデルのアーキテクチャーについてはアクセス対象外となる。

アンソロピックは、セキュアバイオやファカルティーなど他の評価機関との提携は初期段階にあり、アクセス権や公表権は限定的だと述べた。

item.content:encoded:

Thoma Bravo's Proofpoint to buy Varonis Systems in $6.3 billion all-cash deal

Figurines with computers and smartphones are seen in front of the words "Cyber Security" in this illustration taken, February 19, 2024. REUTERS/Dado Ruvic/Illustration

Oct 15 : Thoma Bravo-owned cybersecurity company Proofpoint will buy data security firm Varonis Systems in an all-cash deal valued at about $6.3 billion, the companies said on Thursday. Under the agreement, Varonis shareholders will receive $49.75 per share in cash, a 52 per cent premium to the company's closing share price on June 22, the day before speculation about a possible sale first emerged, the companies said.  The offer values Varonis' equity at $5.71 billion. Its shares rose about 2.7 per cent in extended trading. The deal, expected to close in the first half of 2027, comes as businesses ramp up spending on cybersecurity to combat cybercrime, where AI is being increasingly used to steal data.

Miami-based Varonis offers digital security services, including data classification on cloud storage systems and employee behavior tracking. "Our mission is to secure AI and the data that powers it. By joining forces with Proofpoint, we can achieve this mission faster than ever," Varonis co-founder and CEO Yaki Faitelson said. Reuters had reported in September that Proofpoint was in discussions to acquire Varonis Systems. In June, media outlets had reported that Varonis was weighing a sale after fielding takeover interest from private equity firms, sending the company's shares surging about 30 per cent. Proofpoint, which sells software that helps companies defend against cyberattacks, was bought by Thoma Bravo in 2021 in a take-private deal that valued the company at about $12.3 billion. Goldman Sachs & Co was the financial advisor to Varonis, while BofA Securities, Morgan Stanley & Co, J.P. Morgan Securities, UBS Securities, and Mizuho Securities USA advised Proofpoint. Varonis said it will announce its financial results for the third quarter on November 3, but will not hold an earnings conference call.

item.title: 米国株式市場＝Ｓ＆Ｐ５００上昇、医療株などに資金移動 半導体株は続落
item.description:
Noel Randewich
［１５日 ロイター］ - 米国株式市場はＳ＆Ｐ総合５００種が序盤の下げから持ち直し、上昇...
item.dc:creator: ロイター
item.content:encoded:
米国株式市場＝Ｓ＆Ｐ５００上昇、医療株などに資金移動　半導体株は続落 5:15 配信

2021年7月19日、ニューヨーク証券取引所（NYSE）　REUTERS/Andrew Kelly/File Photo

Noel Randewich

［１５日　ロイター］ - 米国株式市場はＳ＆Ｐ総合５００種が序盤の下げから持ち直し、上昇して取引を終えた。人工知能（ＡＩ）関連株を懸念する投資家が、イーライリリー、ユナイテッドヘルスなどのヘルスケア株やウォルマートなど消費関連株に資金を移した。

ハイテク株の一角は下落した。投資家は、債務負担が大きく金利上昇の影響を受けやすいＡＩ関連企業を精査した。

ドイツ銀行による投資判断の引き上げを受け、イーライリリーは３％超、ユナイテッドヘルスは２．８％、ウォルマートは１．４％それぞれ上昇。この３銘柄がＳ＆Ｐ総合５００種の上昇に大きく寄与した。

エヌビディアは１．８％下落。半導体メーカーの台湾積体電路製造（ＴＳＭＣ）が、ＡＩ関連の旺盛な需要を背景に６四半期連続で過去最高益を記録したものの、２０２７年の見通しについて慎重な見方を示したことを受けた。

サーバーメーカーのデル・テクノロジーズは６．９％、ヒューレット・パッカード・エンタープライズは７．１％それぞれ下落。借り入れコスト上昇の影響を受けやすいＡＩ関連企業への懸念から、両社株は前日の急落に続いて値を下げた。

米１０年債利回りは低下したものの、投資家が原油高に伴うインフレを懸念する中、数年ぶりの高水準近辺にとどまった。

アージェント・キャピタル・マネジメントのポートフォリオマネジャー、ジェド・エラーブルック氏は「新築の一戸建て住宅であれ、巨大なデータセンターであれ、あらゆるものの資金調達コストが上がっており、株式市場のさまざまな分野に影響する」と指摘。「きょう最も好調なのは、景気に左右されにくいディフェンシブ銘柄だ」と述べた。

フィラデルフィア半導体指数は０．９％下落し、７営業日続落となった。

米取引所の合算出来高は２０７億株と、直近２０営業日の平均１７６億株を上回った。

Ｓ＆Ｐ総合５００種の主要１１セクターのうち８セクターが上昇。ヘルスケアが１．８４％高と上昇率で首位となり、素材が１．７１％高で続いた。

宇宙企業ロケット・ラボは６．６％下落した。新型の大型ロケット「ニュートロン」の初打ち上げが２７年に延期されたと発表した。

農薬メーカーのＦＭＣは、第３・四半期の業績見通しを大幅に引き下げたことを受け、３０％超急落した。

Ｓ＆Ｐ総合５００種では値上がり銘柄数が値下がり銘柄数を３．１対１の比率で上回った。

item.title: Petey Halpin, dominant pitchers push Guardians to 2-1 ALCS lead over Rays
item.description: CLEVELAND -- Petey Halpin reacted to the most important hit of his young career by flipping his bat high into the sky. The rest of the Cleveland Guardians saved their wildest celebrations for the postgame.
item.dc:creator: Field Level Media
item.content:encoded: CLEVELAND -- Petey Halpin reacted to the most important hit of his young career by flipping his bat high into the sky. The rest of the Cleveland Guardians saved their wildest celebrations for the postgame. Halpin's go-ahead, two-run homer in the fifth inning off Griffin Jax was the difference in Game 3 of the American League Championship Series, giving Cleveland a 3-2 victory over the Tampa Bay Rays on Thursday afternoon. The Guardians now lead the best-of-seven series 2-1. With the next two games at home, they could wrap up the pennant and book a trip to the World Series without a return to Florida. Halpin's first postseason home run traveled 385 feet over the fence in right, scoring Patrick Bailey to give the Guardians a 3-2 advantage. It was the first homer allowed by Jax since Sept. 9, prompting Halpin to send his bat comically airborne. "I thought I got more of it, I guess, and maybe I was a little tense, so I kind of threw it," Halpin said of the bat flip that ignited the non-sellout crowd of 30,101. "But it's only got to go a little bit over the wall, so that was cool." After Halpin gave AL Central champion Cleveland the lead, its pitching staff took over. Staff ace Gavin Williams and four relievers combined on a three-hitter, striking out 13 to raise their total to 102, an MLB record through eight postseason games. Williams (2-0) struck out nine over five innings, allowing two runs on two hits and a walk. The right-hander leads all postseason pitchers with 33 strikeouts in just 16 2/3 innings over four appearances. "I keep telling myself, 'Don't let the moment get too big,'" Williams said. "I've just got to keep the same routine and keep doing the same thing and I'll be good. "Everybody here is just gritty. That's the big thing. And knowing what you need to do in the right situations." Cade Smith pitched a perfect final 1 1/3 innings for his second save of the series. Daniel Espino, Erik Sabrowski and Hunter Gaddis also saw action as Cleveland began a three-game homestand in the series. Jax (0-1) worked four-plus innings, giving up three runs on five hits. The right-hander struck out two and walked a pair, but was left lamenting his lack of control on the sinker that Halpin sent over the fence. "He does a good job handling off-speed, so it was the right pitch," Jax said. "Just the wrong location." Tampa Bay took a 2-1 lead in the fourth on Chandler Simpson's two-run triple to right. Yandy Diaz and Victor Mesa Jr. scored on the hit that landed just inside the foul line, making Simpson 3-for-6 in his career against Williams. "It was a real good fastball, but I was ready for that," Simpson said. "I got a good pitch that I got the barrel on. The fact that we were down at the time, it gave us a lot of momentum." The Rays' three hits were their fewest in an ALCS game in three appearances. Their 2-1 series deficit is the first time they have trailed in the round after three games. Williams, who carried a no-hitter into the sixth in Game 5 of the AL Division Series against the Chicago White Sox, retired the first nine batters before Diaz doubled leading off the fourth. "Look, we're not a team that strikes out a lot, but I think our swings have actually been pretty good," Diaz said through a translator. "We just need to put the ball in play." Nathaniel Lowe doubled in the second, driving in Jo Adell to put Cleveland up 1-0. Adell had been called out on strikes by umpire Bill Miller, but challenged it and drew a walk. Diaz appeared in his franchise postseason-record 31st game for the Rays. Jax, an Air Force Reserve captain, became the first pitcher to graduate from a United States service academy and start a playoff game. --Brian Dulik, Field Level Media

item.title: Brazil candidates focus fiscal plans on voter-friendly measures before runoff
item.description: As Brazil's presidential runoff campaign enters its final stretch, both candidates are focusing plans for fiscal adjustments on politically palatable measures, reinforcing economists' views that strategies to curb the country's rising debt burden will only come to light after the election.
item.dc:creator: Marcela Ayres
item.content:encoded: As Brazil's presidential runoff campaign enters its final stretch, both candidates are focusing plans for fiscal adjustments on politically palatable measures, reinforcing economists' views that strategies to curb the country's rising debt burden will only come to light after the election. The country's gross debt has risen more than 10 percentage points during President Luiz Inacio Lula da Silva's current term, [USN:L1N45M0ES TEXT:"reaching"] 82.9% of gross domestic product (GDP), as the leftist incumbent seeks reelection after unexpectedly trailing Senator Flavio Bolsonaro in the first round earlier this month. Right-wing Bolsonaro entered the race [USN:L1N4580UE TEXT:"promising"] a faster fiscal adjustment, targeting a 1.5% of GDP improvement in the primary balance within 18 months to trigger a confidence shock and lower borrowing costs. Long-term interest rates have [USN:L1N45R06Y TEXT:"fallen sharply"] since Bolsonaro's first-round victory, reflecting investor optimism about a potential change in government, although his campaign has yet to explain how such an adjustment would be delivered. Lula's campaign has also pledged fiscal consolidation, albeit at a slower pace, while saying that spending cuts should not fall on lower-income Brazilians, a message that has defined the president's economic agenda. With polls [USN:S0N45907Z TEXT:"showing"] Bolsonaro ahead by a narrow margin, both campaigns have stuck to politically safe fiscal proposals, sidestepping measures that would tackle the structural causes of Brazil's worsening fiscal outlook, analysts say. Economists broadly agree that the main challenge lies in the rapid growth of mandatory spending and an increasingly rigid budget. The federal government's discretionary spending accounted for only about 7.6% of total expenditures last year, versus 14.2% in 2000, when Brazil's Federal Budget Panel series began. Bolsonaro's economic adviser Daniella Marques rejected suggestions that a future administration would reduce social benefits, saying pensions and welfare programs would be untouched. "You can make the government work by cutting its own excesses," Marques told broadcaster Band on Wednesday, pointing to things like cuts in political appointments and ministries, among other measures. Lula's running mate Geraldo Alckmin has argued fiscal consolidation should focus on tackling campaign funding and outsized salaries earned by some public-sector workers. Neither campaign has confronted the deeper reforms required to stabilize debt, said Rafaela Vitoria, chief economist at Brazilian lender Inter. "There is no short-term magic solution," she said. "The debate on structural measures is extremely difficult during an election campaign because they are unpopular." Gradual adjustment remains feasible, Vitoria said, adding that discussions over benefit indexation rules, mandatory spending and overlapping social programs will likely have to wait until after the election.

item.title: 米ＦＴＣ、オープンＡＩとアンソロピックに民事召喚状 安全性巡り＝報道
item.description: [１５日 ロイター] - 米連邦取引委員会（ＦＴＣ）が、人工知能（ＡＩ）大手のアンソロピックとオープンＡＩに対し、安全...
item.dc:creator: ロイター
item.content:encoded:
米ＦＴＣ、オープンＡＩとアンソロピックに民事召喚状　安全性巡り＝報道 4:44 配信

2026年6月11日撮影。REUTERS/Dado Ruvic/Illustration/File Photo

[１５日 ロイター] - 米連邦取引委員会（ＦＴＣ）が、人工知能（ＡＩ）大手のアンソロピックとオープンＡＩに対し、安全性に関する事案を巡る文書提出を求める民事召喚状を送付した。米ニュースサイトのアクシオスが事情に詳しい関係者の話として報じた。

ＦＴＣはまた、アンソロピックやオープンＡＩ、研究団体ＭＥＴＲなど、主要なＡＩ開発組織の幹部に証言を求める方針。

オープンＡＩの広報担当者は「ＦＴＣに建設的に対応し、安全水準を引き上げる政策について規制当局や政策立案者との協力を続ける」と述べた。

ＦＴＣとアンソロピックは、アクシオスの報道に関するロイターのコメント要請に直ちに回答しなかった。

アクシオスによると、ＦＴＣの要求書はそれぞれ５０ページを超え、セキュリティー上の問題、安全対策、マーケティング資料、プライバシーポリシーに関する情報を求めている。

ＦＴＣは、不公正な行為などを巡って企業を提訴する広範な権限を持つ。過去にはこの権限を行使し、消費者のデータを保護するための合理的な措置を講じなかった企業に対して法的措置を取ってきた。

item.title: Report: CFP nearing deal to expand to 24 teams in 2027
item.description: The College Football Playoff is nearing a deal to double its number of participating teams from 12 to 24, according to rights holder ESPN.
item.dc:creator: Reuters
item.content:encoded: The College Football Playoff is nearing a deal to double its number of participating teams from 12 to 24, according to rights holder ESPN. The new format would come into effect in 2027 and is pending final approvals, the network reported on Thursday. "Constructive discussions with ESPN continued this week," read a statement from the CFP late Thursday. "We have enjoyed a strong partnership with ESPN since our inception and are appreciative of the productive dialogue we have had throughout the negotiating period and continuing over the last several days. We will provide additional updates on the matters of future format and media rights when appropriate." The playoff's quarterfinals and semifinals are expected to still belong to the New Year's Six bowl games (Rose, Fiesta, Sugar, Peach, Orange, Cotton) within the proposed new format, while the national championship game will likely remain in January. The CFP has used a 12-team format since 2024. From 2014 through 2023, just four teams competed in the postseason event. In March 2024, the CFP and ESPN agreed to a six-year, $7.8 billion contract, giving the network sole media rights through the 2031 season. After months of studying the pros and cons of expansion, the playoff's management committee moved forward with official discussions in September, which are ongoing. In the proposed plan, the top eight seeds receive byes, and seeds 9-16 host seeds 17-24 in the first round. The top eight then host the first-round winners. --Field Level Media

Explainer-Why CoreWeave's troubles are rattling the AI boom

FAST

Oct 15 : CoreWeave's mounting debt is raising fresh concerns about the AI boom, as investors question whether demand can justify the billions being borrowed to build data centres. Shares and bonds of the Nvidia-backed company have tumbled despite its CEO's assurances of a strong contract backlog, fueling a broader selloff in technology stocks. Here is why investors are worried and what its troubles could mean for the industry. WHAT DOES COREWEAVE DO?

CoreWeave rents out computing power from Nvidia processors to companies developing and running AI, including Microsoft and OpenAI. It is one of the leading "neocloud" providers, a group of newer cloud companies that are growing rapidly to meet demand for scarce and expensive AI chips. These neocloud companies give customers access to computing power without requiring them to build their own data centers. However, supplying such capacity requires heavy upfront investment in chips and infrastructure, often financed with debt. WHAT IS ITS FINANCIAL SITUATION? The company, which has never turned a profit, has about $50 billion in debt, according to data compiled by LSEG. It raised its annual capital spending forecast by $4 billion in August to between $35 billion and $39 billion. Analysts expect revenue of nearly $13 billion this year and a loss of $2.13 billion. The yields on its bonds due in 2031, which are rated junk, have spiked to about 16 per cent, while the cost of insuring its debt against default has climbed to about 1,000 basis points, reflecting growing concern among creditors. CEO Mike Intrator told employees in an internal memo seen by Reuters that its deal backlog more than covers its debt obligations. The company had a $104.2 billion revenue backlog at the end of the second quarter, followed by more than $25 billion in new commitments early in the third quarter. Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang has also downplayed the concerns, saying CoreWeave's financial strength is improving and he sees no need to backstop it. The chip giant has agreed to buy unsold CoreWeave capacity through April 2032. WHY IT COULD BE A CANARY IN THE COAL MINE CoreWeave's business depends on two things: demand for AI computing and lenders' willingness to finance the infrastructure supplying it. But a selloff in its shares suggests a lack of confidence among investors in the latter, even as the company cites strong demand. The concern is not that AI demand will collapse, but that higher borrowing costs could make the business harder to sustain if demand were to weaken sharply. "It looks more like investors questioning how the build-out is being funded than a sudden collapse in appetite for AI computing," said Axel Rudolph, chief technical analyst at IG Group. "CoreWeave is quickly becoming the AI trade's canary in the coal mine," said Kathleen Brooks, research director at XTB. WHY ARE MARKETS FRETTING? Investors are questioning whether AI revenue can grow fast enough to cover the cost of building and financing the infrastructure. CoreWeave has to spend heavily upfront before it can collect the revenue from its contracts. Higher interest rates could drive up financing costs and further squeeze returns. The hardware itself poses another risk. Chips lose value as newer generations arrive, pushing providers to spend even more to replace them. The concerns, however, go beyond CoreWeave. US technology giants are expected to spend more than $700 billion on AI infrastructure this year. THE DOWNSIDE SCENARIO One potential consequence would be a broader financing squeeze, with lenders demanding higher returns or becoming less willing to fund other AI projects. That could force providers to scale back expansion, curbing equipment purchases and affecting the computing capacity customers expect. A setback could also deepen doubts that the AI investment frenzy is outpacing returns, piling further pressure on technology stocks. The impact of the fallout would depend on how the business is reorganized, and CoreWeave's ties to major technology companies do not, by themselves, mean its failure would trigger a wider financial crisis. WHO ELSE BEARS THE RISK? Gartner estimates about 80 per cent of neoclouds could shut down by 2030, warning that expected AI revenue will not support profitable returns on all planned infrastructure spending. Neocloud rivals Nebius, Applied Digital and Iren have fallen in the recent selloff. The cost of default protection has risen for SoftBank, which is betting heavily on OpenAI. Meanwhile, spreads for Amazon, Alphabet, Meta and Nvidia have also reached records, although they have risen much more slowly than CoreWeave's. However, these companies also have larger cash flows and stronger balance sheets.

Source: Reuters

item.title: Indian mutual funds stop bulk subscriptions to gold ETFs ahead of festive season
item.description: Several large Indian mutual funds issued public notices late on Thursday suspending bulk subscriptions to gold exchange-traded funds, just ahead of the festive season when investor demand typically rises.
item.dc:creator: Ira Dugal, Rajendra Jadhav
item.content:encoded: Several large Indian mutual funds issued public notices late on Thursday suspending bulk subscriptions to gold exchange-traded funds, just ahead of the festive season when investor demand typically rises. The notices from the fund houses, including Kotak Mahindra Mutual Fund, UTI Mutual Fund and HDFC Mutual Fund, did not cite a reason for the move. There is no restriction on redemptions from these funds. The decision was taken following a nudge from the Securities and Exchange Board of India, according to a mutual fund executive familiar with the discussions. Two bullion industry officials confirmed the halt had followed discussions with the market regulator. The sources declined to be identified as they are not permitted to comment on discussions with the regulator. A spokesperson for SEBI did not respond to a Reuters request for comment outside business hours. The [USN:L1N45X01Q TEXT:"Indian rupee has been under pressure this year"] due to a surge in global oil prices, which have inflated the country's import bill, and heavy selling by foreign investors in Indian equities. Strong demand for gold has further weighed on the currency, prompting the government to raise import duties on gold and silver earlier this year. India, the world's largest consumer of silver and second-largest consumer of gold, relies on imports to meet most of its demand, a dependence that can sometimes widen its trade deficit. Gold imports fell to $1.8 billion in September, from $2.3 billion in August. However, Indians will celebrate Dussehra in October and Diwali in early November, when buying gold is considered auspicious. Inflows into gold and silver ETFs surged during last year's festive season as investors turned to precious metals amid lackluster stock market returns. The move is surprising, as gold and silver imports have fallen sharply over the past two months from a year earlier and have not contributed to the trade deficit, said a dealer at a private bank that supplies bullion to ETFs. "It looks more like a precautionary measure to avoid a surge in imports in October," the dealer said.

item.dc:creator: ロイター
item.content:encoded:
欧州市場サマリー（15日） 3:42 配信

＜ロンドン株式市場＞

続伸して取引を終えた。ヒーリー英財務相が財政規律重視の姿勢を示したことが好感され、ＦＴＳＥ１００種は約１カ月半ぶりの高値を付けた。中型株で構成するＦＴＳＥ２５０種指数は０．２６％上昇した。人工知能（ＡＩ）関連株の売り圧力が強まる中、日用品や医薬品株が物色された。

ヒーリー氏は今月発表する予算案は経済の強化を目指すとし、財政規律重視の方針でバーナム首相と一致していると言及した。

製薬大手アストラゼネカは３．２％、ＧＳＫは２．９％それぞれ上昇。日用品のユニリーバは１．８％、ブリティッシュ・アメリカン・タバコは２．５％値上がりした。

ＦＴＳＥ３５０種銀行株指数は０．３０％高。

銅価格の下落を受けて、鉱業株指数は１．３９％安。銅大手アントファガスタは４．１％値下がりした。

製紙・包装大手のモンディは７．９％下落した。

８月の英国内総生産（ＧＤＰ）は前月比０．１％増と、予想に反してプラス成長となった。イングランド銀行（英中央銀行）チーフエコノミストのピル氏は、中銀が今後利上げに踏み切ったとしても、連続利上げの始まりと解釈すべきでないと述べた。ロイター調査によると、市場では１１月会合での利上げ決定を予想している。

ロンドン株式市場：[.LJP]

＜欧州株式市場＞

続伸して取引を終えた。堅調な企業決算が好感された。ヘルスケア株が買われる一方、ハイテク株は売り注文が優勢だった。

スウェーデン通信機器大手エリクソンは６．８％高。直近四半期の業績が市場予想を上回り、買われた。

ＳＴＯＸＸ欧州６００種ヘルスケア株指数は２．３８％上昇。一方、テクノロジー株指数は１．４８％下落。ドイツの半導体製造装置メーカー、アイクストロンは１２．７％安と急落。ドイツの半導体大手インフィニオン・テクノロジーズは５．２％、フランスの半導体材料大手ソイテックは７．７％それぞれ下落。オランダの半導体製造装置メーカーＡＳＭＬホールディングは４．２％下落した。

銅価格の値下がりを受けて、資源株指数は０．８４％下落した。

ＬＳＥＧのデータによると、市場では、欧州中央銀行（ＥＣＢ）が１２月の理事会で利上げを決めるとの観測が強まっている。

欧州株式市場：[.FJ]

＜ユーロ圏債券＞

指標となるドイツ１０年国債の利回りが約５週間ぶりの低水準を付けた。人工知能（ＡＩ）を巡る懸念から株式が売られ、投資家が安全資産の国債に資金を移した。

フランスおよびイタリアの国債と独国債の利回り格差は縮小し、この日の動きが安全資産への逃避だけによるものではないことを示唆した。原油価格の下落も利回り低下圧力となった。

ユーロ圏の指標となる独１０年債利回りは１１ベーシスポイント（ｂｐ）低下の３．３５６％。１日の低下幅としては４月以来の大きさとなる見通し。

ここ数カ月、財政の持続可能性に対する投資家の懸念が、特に債務負担の大きい国で国債利回りを押し上げていたが、債券市場の緊張は和らぎ始めている。

仏１０年債利回りは１４ｂｐ低下の４．７３９％。１日の低下幅としては５月以来の大きさとなる見通し。

独仏１０年債利回り格差は４．５ｂｐ縮小の１３７ｂｐ。フランスの財政の先行きへの懸念から、１０月初めには１５８．６７ｂｐと、２０１１年１１月以来の高水準に拡大していた。

イタリア１０年債と独国債の利回り格差は４ｂｐ縮小の１０４ｂｐ。同様に１０月初めには１２９．７４ｂｐと、２０２５年４月以来の高水準に拡大していた。

政策金利見通しに敏感な独２年債利回りは７ｂｐ低下の３．０３５％となった。

item.description: At a G20 finance ministers’ meeting in Bangkok, German Finance Minister Lars Klingbeil said, “There will be no pretending that Russia is now returning as a normal member of the G20 and simply taking its seat at the table again - not with me, and not with the other Europeans.”

Germany warns against bringing Russia back into G20 fold

At a G20 finance ministers’ meeting in Bangkok, German Finance Minister Lars Klingbeil said, “There will be no pretending that Russia is now returning as a normal member of the G20 and simply taking its seat at the table again - not with me, and not with the other Europeans.”

German Finance Minister Lars Klingbeil speaks during the annual review meeting of the "Made for Germany" initiative, at Siemens AG in Berlin, Germany Sep 30, 2026. (Photo: REUTERS/Annegret Hilse)

FAST

BANGKOK: Germany warned on Thursday (Oct 15) against efforts to bring Russia back on to the international stage, while Britain called for tighter sanctions on Russia n shipping, as questions grow about the strength of US support for Ukraine. Russia n Finance Minister Anton Siluanov attended a meeting of G20 finance ministers and central bankers in Bangkok, just over a month after the US had hosted his first in-person G20 appearance since Russia invaded Ukraine, at a meeting in Asheville, North Carolina. "I do notice attempts, particularly from the United States ... to bring Russia back onto the international stage," German Finance Minister Lars Klingbeil told reporters. "There will be no pretending that Russia is now returning as a normal member of the G20 and simply taking its seat at the table again - not with me, and not with the other Europeans."

RIFT OVER RUSSIA SANCTIONS US Treasury Undersecretary Erin Browne said Washington supported Russia's presence, noting that allies had not raised their concerns directly with the US delegation this week. "We think it's really important if you're going to solve a crisis, you need to have open dialogue and open conversation," she told Reuters. "And you can't have ... dialogue, and you can't have resolution to conflict if no one's talking to one another." US President Donald Trump remained committed to bringing about a peaceful end to the war between Russia and Ukraine, she said. British finance minister John Healey called on other nations to tighten sanctions on Russia -linked shipping. "My message to finance ministers here today ... on Ukraine, is to stay the path on tough economic sanctions on Russia , especially a tighter ban on shipping services ... that help ( Russia n President Vladimir) Putin's sanctions-busting shadow fleet to operate," he said. Britain has imposed a series of sanctions on shipping and related services that it believes Russia uses to fund and equip its war on Ukraine.

Related:

Commentary: Trump’s Russian diesel U-turn comes at bad time for Ukraine

Ukraine accuses US of helping Russia as missiles hit Kyiv

NATO general sets out tough military response to any 'foolish' Russian attack

However, a US official said on Wednesday the Trump administration was considering easing sanctions on these vessels, which have transported oil and petroleum products from countries including Russia , Iran and Venezuela. The differences extend beyond sanctions. German Chancellor Friedrich Merz said on Thursday that Europe would retain control of Russia n sovereign assets frozen after Moscow's invasion of Ukraine, rejecting any suggestion they could be transferred to a US-supervised vehicle as part of a peace initiative. US President Donald Trump temporarily lifted sanctions on Russia n diesel fuel , a move met with criticism from Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelenskyy, European countries and some of Trump's fellow Republicans in the US Senate. Trump's envoys told Ukrainian officials last week that the diesel deal was part of an effort to draw Russia back to negotiations after the failure of previous efforts to launch sustained talks to end the war. "It is always useful for talks to take place. But I want to be very clear that these talks must not come at Ukraine's expense, or take place over the heads of the Ukrainian people or President Zelenskyy," Klingbeil said.

EU SEEKS TO RAISE FUNDS FOR UKRAINE The EU has pledged €45 billion (US$50 billion) for Ukraine in 2027, but the country's needs will be much higher and the EU is scrambling to organise financial support from countries such as Norway, Switzerland, Canada, Japan and Britain. Klingbeil said he was discussing with international partners how to ensure Ukraine's financing, with commitments from Australia and South Korea made during meetings on Thursday. Healey said Britain would provide £17 million (US$23 million) in funding towards repairs for Ukraine's Chornobyl nuclear power plant, which had been damaged by a Russia n drone strike last year, alongside support from the US and France.

Source: Reuters/fs

SAN FRANCISCO, Oct 15 : Amazon unveiled two new devices on Thursday for listening to and recording people's information throughout the day to offer calendar reminders and other AI-driven insights under the Bee brand it acquired last year. Frontier is a bracelet and Eclipse is a brick that resembles a portable magnetic charger. Users attach the Eclipse to their smartphones. The devices aggregate information from calendars, apps and other data throughout the day, Amazon said.  The Frontier bracelet costs $75 and the Eclipse $100, Amazon said. "They listen to your whole day," said Amazon devices chief Panos Panay at the TechCrunch Disrupt conference in San Francisco. "It reminds you of the conversations you had, it reminds you of to-dos that you may have had, it tells you that you have some action items that you committed to other people."

USERS CONTROL PRIVACY: AMAZON He said that because the devices are always listening when turned on, users do not have to make reminders for themselves and "can stay more present" throughout the day. The company said users control privacy by deciding when to turn it on and can delete insights or prior conversations as they see fit. Amazon does not store audio.  The company faced criticism after reports in 2019 that thousands of people were listening to conversations people had with its Alexa voice assistant service. It is facing a class action lawsuit over the practice. Amazon has denied any wrongdoing. Bee will retain data for 14 days, though users can extend that by paying for a $12-per-month subscription. The devices can also connect to Alexa+, Amazon's subscription generative AI voice service. Amazon's Bee will face competition in AI wearables, notably Meta's Muse Charm, a pendant using the company's latest agentic AI software, and its eyeglasses with cameras and other sensors. A host of startups have also developed similar devices, designed to record conversations and take action on behalf of users. In recent weeks, Amazon has announced a flurry of new gadgets, part of Panay's effort to attract buyers willing to spend more for higher quality and durability. A slate of tablets Amazon announced last week costs as much as three times more than prior versions, despite slowing global sales of the portable computers. Reuters reported earlier this year that Amazon is considering a return to the smartphone market about a decade after the release of its failed Fire Phone.

Oct 15 : Anthropic has given nonprofit METR employee-level access to its systems and is in talks with others including Hugging Face, as AI companies pitch external evaluators as a way to safely advance the technology without slowing its development. The developer of Claude models is also working with biosecurity nonprofit SecureBio and Accenture's AI business Faculty as evaluators, it said in a blog post on Thursday. Reuters exclusively reported earlier this week that Anthropic and OpenAI had sought significant control over what outside reviewers could publish, concerned that the findings could leak trade secrets. A person familiar with the matter told Reuters that talks with Anthropic had evolved recently, with the company becoming more open in negotiations.

A key sticking point between evaluators and AI labs is that information the companies might consider crucial intellectual property can also be relevant to assessing a model's risks, leading to disputes and redactions, a separate person familiar with the discussions told Reuters. Experts have also said the independence of evaluators is a concern, as Anthropic and OpenAI choose who gets to carry out the reviews. The outcome of the talks will help determine how the world scrutinizes a technology that some of its creators warn may be advancing beyond humanity's ability to manage. THE METR TIE-UP Anthropic said on Thursday six employees of METR — or Model Evaluation and Threat Research — have company hardware, office space and access to internal systems roughly equivalent to its risk assessment teams. However, customer data, legally privileged information and model architecture will remain off limits. The company said it cannot veto METR's findings on risks, incidents and practices, but can require narrowly defined redactions. METR can also publicly question those redactions without revealing the withheld information. "In line with our transparency policies, our report will openly describe the scope, access, and other limitations of our work," METR said. The nonprofit had proposed on Wednesday that developers allow private staff interviews, timely publication of assessments and transparency about access limits and redactions. Anthropic said its other evaluator partnerships are at an early stage, with more limited access and publication rights.  The company is developing three tiers of access. Evaluators at the first level will conduct narrowly scoped investigations and need approval to publish. Those at the second will receive more information and can publish without approval, subject to redactions evaluators can publicly challenge. The third, used by METR, provides employee-like access with similar publication rights to the second tier. SecureBio is in the first tier and is reviewing the chemical and biological weapons chapter of Anthropic's August risk report, having published a pilot review of the previous report. Anthropic said it would consider expanding SecureBio's access and publication rights after the review. Anthropic also announced last month that it is working on a tie-up with Faculty covering model evaluations, adversarial testing and assessments of whether models behave as intended, among other areas.

Source: Reuters

item.title: India markets regulator partly reverses derivative settlement rules after pushback
item.description: India's markets regulator said on Thursday it would use volume-weighted average prices (VWAP) from the final 30 minutes of regular trading to settle expiring stock and index derivatives contracts, reversing its decision to use closing auction prices.
item.dc:creator: Jayshree Pyasi, Bharath Rajeswaran, Vivek M
item.content:encoded: India's markets regulator said on Thursday it would use volume-weighted average prices (VWAP) from the final 30 minutes of regular trading to settle expiring stock and index derivatives contracts, reversing its decision to use closing auction prices. The closing auction session (CAS) will continue to determine the closing prices of applicable cash-equity securities, the Securities and Exchange Board of India (SEBI) said in a circular. CAS, implemented by SEBI from August 3, had triggered a backlash from traders after sharp swings in stock and index levels during the close. Erratic movements in the expiring derivatives contracts propelled traders to pull back on volumes. Reuters [USN:L1N45R0C2 TEXT:"reported"] last week that SEBI was considering reverting to 30-minute VWAP-based settlements for expiring derivatives contracts. The changes will be effective from December 7. CAS will operate as a separate 10-minute session from 3:30 p.m. to 3:40 p.m. on all trading days. Order entry will close randomly between 3:38 p.m. and 3:40 p.m. Traders can enter both limit and market orders from 3:31 p.m. to 3:36 p.m., after which they may place only limit orders. A market order is executed immediately at the best available price, while a limit order is executed only at the investor's specified price or better. Expiring index derivatives will cease trading at 3:30 p.m. on expiry days. Stock derivatives will continue to trade until 3:45 p.m. on all trading days, including expiry days. The cash-market post-close session will run from 3:50 p.m. to 4 p.m., with trades executed at the closing price.

Oct 15 : Skydance's CNN, the Financial Times, Axios and other publishers joined Google's AI news program to license their content for generative AI features and explore ways to drive audience engagement. The search-engine giant said on Thursday that the program, which started as a pilot last year with partners like The Washington Post, now includes more than 400 publications globally. The deal marks CNN's first partnership since Paramount Skydance completed its acquisition of Warner Bros Discovery, as CEO David Ellison seeks to position the combined company as a technology-driven media business. As part of these agreements, publishers will provide enhanced content rights, allowing Google to develop new AI features, while Google will pay participating news organizations for their content. Financial terms were not disclosed.

"Google's innovation with generative AI has changed how people discover information and content, and now those tools will help us explore new ways to discover and engage audiences," said Sam Felix, CNN's senior vice president of strategic partnerships and business development. Google said the AI features will come with clear attribution and direct links, helping readers to connect with the sources they value. The announcement comes at a time when publishers are stepping up legal efforts to prevent AI companies from using their content without permission to train large language models. News publishers are also grappling with declining referral traffic as search engines roll out AI-generated answers that allow users to consume information without clicking through to websites. CNN said the deal is in line with its strategy to protect its intellectual property, adding that it has multiple commercial partnerships and ongoing discussions with other industry players. The network operates television, streaming and digital news services worldwide, including CNN International and CNN Originals, as well as a direct-to-consumer subscription service and CNN Newsource.

NEW YORK: The Nasdaq fell to near one-month lows on Thursday (Oct 15), weighed by a worsening selloff in AI-linked stocks on fears rising interest rates could impact artificial-intelligence investments, and fresh data pointing to building US price pressures. The S&P 500 and the Nasdaq marked their biggest one-day fall since July on Wednesday after hotter-than-expected consumer inflation data fuelled expectations of further interest- rate hikes from the US Federal Reserve, dragging on tech stocks. S emiconductor maker TSMC 's cautious note for 2027, citing macroeconomic uncert ai nties, also dented sentiment. Reports that AI lab Anthropic' s third-quarter revenue surged 45 per cent compared to the previous quarter failed to lift investor spirits.

Heavily indebted data-centre operator CoreWeave sitting in the eye of the recent tech storm, lost 8.5 per cent fol low ing a 15 per cent drop on Wednesday , while c loud computing giant Oracle was down marginally after a near ly 9 per cent fall in the previous session. The companies' bonds also fell, pushing their yields to record highs. Chipmakers lost ground, with Nvidia down 3.3 per cent, and Micron Technology and Advanced Micro Devices losing 5 per cent and 6.4 per cent, respectively. The broader chips index will have shed US$2 trillion in a more-than-14 per cent slide in seven sessions, if losses hold. It would mark its longest losing streak since May 2025. The S&P 500 information technology sector was the biggest drag, down 2 per cent. The slump pushed investors to government bonds, with the benchmark 10-year US Treasury yield at a three-week low of 5.0725 per cent. " Investors are increasingly questioning how much future growth is already priced into valuations, how expansion is being financed and when these investments will generate sufficient returns," Charu Chanana, chief investment strategist at Saxo, said in a note. "The repricing of CoreWeave's debt suggests that investors are becoming less willing to finance AI infrastructure growth at any cost."

Related:

Commentary: Every investment portfolio looks like the same trade - AI

At 9:50am ET (11:50pm, Singapore time), the Dow J one s Industrial Average rose 163.58 points, or 0.32 per cent, to 51,785.06, the S&P 500 shed 32 .20 points, or 0.42 per cent, to 7,686.74, and the Nasdaq Composite .IXIC lost 283.07 points, or 1.06 per cent, to 26,409.80. The CBOE Volatility Index, known as Wall Street's fear gauge, hit a two-week high and was last up 0.83 points at 17.74. Investors continued to segue into traditionally defensive sectors, with healthcare .SPXHC and consumer staples .SPLRCS rising more than 2 per cent each. Gains in these stocks propped up the Dow. The Nasdaq has dropped more than 4 per cent from record highs touched last week, with concerns about higher borrowing costs and AI spending threatening to eclipse the third-quarter earnings season, when S&P 500 profits are expected to grow 30.6 per cent, according to LSEG data. Data showed US producer prices increased by the most in 4-1/2 years in September amid rising goods and services costs, the latest indication of inflation broadening out beyond energy products. Markets will now scrutinize Fed Ch ai r Kevin Warsh's speech before the International M one tary Fund Annual Meeting. Shares of Rocket Lab dropped 1 5 per cent after the space company s ai d the inaugural launch of its new, larger Neutron rocket was delayed until next year. FMC slid over 38 per cent after the agrichemicals company sharply cut its third-quarter outlook, which includes a US$625 million-US$675 million hit from commercial actions. Advancing issues outnumbered decliners by a 1.78-to-1 ratio on the NYSE and by a 1.05-to-1 ratio on the Nasdaq. The S&P 500 posted 20 new 52-week highs and no new lows, while the Nasdaq Composite recorded 29 new highs and 261 new lows.

Source: Reuters/fs

item.description: [バンコク １５日 ロイター] - 日本の財務省同行筋によると、主要７カ国（Ｇ７）と２０カ国・地域（Ｇ２０）の会合に...
item.dc:creator: ロイター
item.content:encoded:
Ｇ７・Ｇ２０当局者、金融不安の切迫リスク認めず＝日本の財務省同行筋 1:45 配信

タイ・バンコクで開催されたＩＭＦ・世銀総会に出席した当局者ら　REUTERS/Patipat Janthong

[バンコク １５日 ロイター] - 日本の財務省同行筋によると、主要７カ国（Ｇ７）と２０カ国・地域（Ｇ２０）の会合に出席した財務当局トップらは、最近の人工知能（ＡＩ）関連の市場急落によって金融システムが不安定化する差し迫ったリスクはないとの認識を示した。最近の株式市場の動向を特に取り上げて議論することはなかったという。

会合に出席した財務省同行筋は記者団に対し、両会合では、世界経済が外部からのショックに対して底堅さを示していることを前提に議論が行われたと説明した。ただ、政策当局者らは警戒を怠らず、金融システム危機の芽を放置しない必要性を確認したという。

さらに同筋は、市場動向は常に注意深く監視しているとしながらも、株式、為替、債券市場の個々の動きについてはコメントしないとした。

BERLIN, Oct 15 : Germany plans a wide-ranging cooperation agreement with US chip maker Nvidia to boost the take-up of artificial intelligence in German industry, business daily Handelsblatt said on Thursday, citing people familiar with the issue. It said the deal would be announced next week at the Invest in Germany conference in Berlin, where Nvidia Chief Executive Jensen Huang will be a guest. The aim of the deal would be two-fold, the newspaper said. Firstly, it would create the basis for physical AI tools, used in training robots or self-driving vehicles. Secondly, it would help to create high-performance AI models for industry. The newspaper said the agreement would involve investments in the hundreds of millions of euros.

FAST

WASHINGTON, Oct 15 : Nvidia and Apple each committed $25 million for US President Donald Trump's planned White House ballroom, according to a Washington Post report on Thursday that showed $333 million in private donations for the project. The Adelson family, longtime financial supporters of Trump and his Republican Party, committed $25 million as well, as did billionaire Charles Ergen, co-founder and chairman of telecommunications company Dish Network, the report added.  The president himself is not on the list, according to the Post. Reuters has not verified the report. The White House said it would not release information about the donors, who spokesman Davis Ingle said "represent a wide array of great American companies."

"The same critics who are alleging fake conflicts of interests would also complain if American taxpayers were footing the bill for these long-overdue renovations," Ingle told Reuters. Nvidia said it was proud to make a donation to a nonpartisan trust that serves Americans. "As an American company, our support for the United States is paramount, and independent of any business interests," a spokesperson said. Apple declined to comment. The scale of the ballroom project and the administration’s handling of fundraising and disclosures have drawn criticism from watchdog groups and legal experts, who say they raise questions about transparency, donor influence and adherence to longstanding ethics and oversight norms. "The secrecy is a huge problem," said Eric Petry of the Brennan Center for Justice. "When people with business before the government can give millions to the president's pet project, and the public can't see who or how much, there's no way to tell whether they're buying access or favors." Federal contractors including Lockheed Martin Corp, Microsoft Corp and Palantir Technologies Inc all gave $10 million, the Post reported. The companies did not immediately respond to a request for comment. Trump initially said he and wealthy donors would pay for the estimated $400 million project, but he later unsuccessfully sought $1 billion from Congress for an underground bunker and security features to harden the facility. The Post reported that the "vast majority of the funds raised came from companies and wealthy individuals with interests before the federal government" and that half the total came from companies or executives of firms that have had federal government contracts in Trump's second White House term. The planned ballroom is among several projects Trump is pursuing in his efforts to remake Washington with sweeping, unilateral changes that his opponents have challenged in court and called a power grab. The US Supreme Court, in a 5-4 ruling in August, allowed Trump to continue construction of the ballroom while he challenges a judicial order that would halt much of the development. In a dissent, Chief Justice John Roberts said the project was "likely unlawful." The ballroom, which Trump has said will seat 1,000 guests, has faced public backlash. Preservationists and opponents say Trump exceeded his authority by demolishing the historic East Wing, which housed the first lady's offices and the White House movie theater, to make room for the structure. Trump says a planned 90,000-square-foot (8,360-square-meter) White House ballroom will include bomb shelters, medical facilities, defenses against drones and missiles and other security features. Confronted with criticism of the project, his administration now says the facility is needed for national security, an argument the president has also made about a proposed triumphal arch.

Source: Reuters

item.title: 米企業在庫 8月は前月比0.4％増 予想と一致
item.description: [ワシントン １５日 ロイター] - 米商務省が１５日発表した８月の企業在庫は、前月比０．４％増加し、エコノミスト予想...
item.dc:creator: ロイター
item.content:encoded:
米企業在庫　8月は前月比0.4％増　予想と一致 0:24 配信

米イリノイ州グレンビューのＡＢＴエレクトロニクスの施設。2018年12月撮影。 REUTERS/Richa Naidu

[ワシントン　１５日　ロイター] - 米商務省が１５日発表した８月の企業在庫は、前月比０．４％増加し、エコノミスト予想と一致した。売上高が堅調に伸びる中、在庫も緩やかな増加となった。

前年同月比では４．６％増加した。企業は、個人消費や人工知能（ＡＩ）投資に主に支えられた堅調な国内需要を背景に５四半期連続で在庫を取り崩した後、積み増しに転じている。ただ、在庫積み増しの大部分は輸入に依存しており、国内総生産（ＧＤＰ）成長率の押し下げ要因となっている。

８月の小売在庫は０．２％増加した。先月公表された速報値の０．３％増から下方改定された。７月は０．９％増だった。自動車在庫は０．８％増と速報値から変わらず。７月は１．０％増だった。

ＧＤＰ算出に用いられる自動車を除く小売在庫は横ばいとなり、先月公表された速報値の０．１％増から下方改定された。７月は０．８％増だった。

卸売在庫と製造業者の在庫は０．５％、それぞれ増加した。

企業売上高は１．１％増加。前月は０．５％増だった。

８月の販売ペースに基づく在庫解消に必要な期間は１．３３カ月と、７月の１．３４カ月から短縮した。前年同月は１．４０カ月だった。

ロイター 関連ニュース 焦点：米景気拡大維持、ＦＲＢの利下げペース次第 アングル：出遅れ気味の米不動産株、持ち直し期待高まる 焦点：後退する米企業役員の多様性、トランプ米大統領の政策反映 コラム：「米国例外主義」なお健在、外国投資家のテック株流入持続が示唆 アングル：米株、下半期の上昇基調維持に多くの試練　ＡＩ投資から金融政策まで 最終更新: 10/16(金) 0:24 ロイター

item.title: FBI, US Postal Service investigate suspicious mailings to election officials, lawmakers
item.description: The FBI and US Postal Service's law enforcement arm said on Thursday they were investigating suspicious mailings, including some sent to state election officials and lawmakers' offices ahead of the November 3 midterm elections.
item.dc:creator: David Shepardson
item.content:encoded: The FBI and US Postal Service's law enforcement arm said on Thursday they were investigating suspicious mailings, including some sent to state election officials and lawmakers' offices ahead of the November 3 midterm elections. The FBI said some of the letters contained an unknown substance. The investigation come less than three weeks before the midterms, which will determine control of the US Congress, as the Postal Service prepares to handle millions of mailed ballots. Spokespeople for Senate Democratic Leader Chuck Schumer, Alex Padilla, a California Democrat, and Chris Murphy, a Connecticut Democrat, all said the US Postal Service intercepted letters containing a suspicious substance mailed to their offices. "This incident is a stark reminder of the very real dangers facing those who serve the public and who help administer our elections," Padilla said in a statement. The US House of Representatives sergeant at arms, the House's chief law enforcement officer, told staff in an email seen by Reuters that some public officials had received letters containing suspicious white powder substances. Brendan Donahue, a deputy chief inspector with the US Postal Inspection Service, said some suspicious letters had been intercepted and that an investigation was ongoing. "We are committed to protecting our nation's election officials from threatening and dangerous mail. Any threat or attack on an election official is unacceptable," Donahue told reporters. The National Association of Secretaries of State and the National Association of State Election Directors said late on Wednesday a series of suspicious letters was sent to state election offices. Letters bound for several state election offices were intercepted before they were delivered, including in Pennsylvania, Ohio and Idaho. The Wisconsin Elections Commission said on Thursday it received a suspicious letter with an unidentified powdery substance that was deemed not hazardous. "Let this be very clear: this incident will not shake us,” said Meagan Wolfe, the state’s chief election official. An email to Senate staff said suspicious letters could have postmarks that do not match the return address and included an image of an envelope with a return address labeled "DSA" and a New York City address. POSTAL SERVICE PLANS NEW MEASURES Earlier on Thursday, US Postmaster General David Steiner said USPS was "absolutely ready" to handle millions of ballots for the midterm elections. USPS said this month it would take "extraordinary measures" for the 2026 election, including extending hours at some retail locations and expediting handling, extra deliveries and special pickups of ballots. On September 14, the US Supreme Court declined to let USPS enforce a rule targeting mail-in ballots, dealing a setback to President Donald Trump's effort to restrict voting by mail. USPS said it would not enforce the rule under the order. The agency adopted the measure after Trump issued a March executive order aimed at tightening rules governing mail voting. In 2024, USPS delivered 99.2 million ballots to and from voters in the presidential election. About 30% of votes were cast by mail in the November 2024 presidential election, down from 46% in 2020. Trump's fellow Republicans are locked in a tight battle to retain control of Congress in the midterms. Democratic voters disproportionately use mail-in ballots, according to various surveys, so restricting them could benefit Republicans. Under the rule that was blocked, states would have had to provide lists of mail-ballot recipients to USPS and use agency-approved outbound and return ballot mail envelopes outfitted with unique barcodes. The Postal Service could then have refused to send out ballots that did not comply or were associated with voters not appearing on the lists.

item.title: US delays small imports rule that raised alarm over prescription drug costs
item.description: The US government has delayed by 90 days implementation of new customs requirements for small international mail shipments, a move that should forestall higher prices for imported prescription drugs and other products for inflation-weary Americans until after the November midterm elections.
item.dc:creator: Kamal Choudhury
item.content:encoded: The US government has delayed by 90 days implementation of new customs requirements for small international mail shipments, a move that should forestall higher prices for imported prescription drugs and other products for inflation-weary Americans until after the November midterm elections . The US Customs and Border Protection rule targets the [USN:L1N44A13F TEXT:"de minimis tariffs exemption"], which has eased requirements for shipments under $800. The rule aimed to speed up implementation of changes authorized by US lawmakers as part of President Donald Trump's spending and tax-cut bill, which are due to take effect in July 2027. The agency said on Wednesday it has pushed the mandatory compliance date for a new mail entry process to January 20, 2027, from October 22. That prior deadline was just 12 days before the November 3 elections in which US households' affordability woes are a central issue dogging Trump's Republican Party with control of Congress up for grabs. It said there would be no changes to international mail entry procedures before then. The process requires electronic filing for postal shipments subject to Section 201, 232 or 301 duties, or under the jurisdiction of a partner government agency such as the US Food and Drug Administration. It also involves a customs bond. As the October 22 deadline approached, patient advocates and industry groups had warned the rule's data and bonding requirements could cause delays, refusals or added costs for personal drug orders. IMPACT ON PHARMA The FDA officially bars individuals from importing foreign prescription drugs, but it has discretion in limited circumstances. Some Americans order medicines from other countries like Canada, where the cost of drugs can be sharply lower. The Canadian International Pharmacy Association has said most routine personal orders from licensed foreign pharmacies could be disrupted. A separate letter signed by 71 members of Congress, led by Democratic Representatives Jan Schakowsky of Illinois and Wisconsin's Mark Pocan, asked agencies to delay the procedures for prescription medicines unless personal-use drugs were assured. “For patients concerned about losing access to lower-cost prescriptions from abroad, this delay is a welcome reprieve, but not a permanent solution," said Merith Basey, CEO of Patients For Affordable Drugs. "Until patients in the US can get access to the prescription drugs they need at prices they can afford, disrupting existing personal-importation practices risks an important safety valve.” The Department of Health and Human Services referred questions to CBP, which did not immediately respond to a request for comment on whether personal-use exemptions are planned. CBP said the extension gives importers, brokers and logistics providers more time to update processes, helps avoid disruptions and will close gaps that have been exploited by smugglers. CBP's announcement did not mention medicines, and the rule does not name them.

item.title: コアウィーブ株再び急落、25年5月以来安値 ＡＩ投資に債務懸念
item.description:
Aditya Soni Anhata Rooprai
[１５日 ロイター] - 人工知能（ＡＩ）向けクラウドサービスを...
item.dc:creator: ロイター
item.content:encoded:
コアウィーブ株再び急落、25年5月以来安値　ＡＩ投資に債務懸念 0:03 配信

コアウィーブのロゴ。7月20日撮影のイメージ写真。REUTERS/Dado Ruvic

Aditya Soni　Anhata Rooprai

[１５日 ロイター] - 人工知能（ＡＩ）向けクラウドサービスを提供するコアウィーブの株式と社債が１５日、再び急落した。最高経営責任者（ＣＥＯ）が受注残の多さを強調したにもかかわらず、借入金による資金調達にますます依存するＡＩインフラの拡充を巡り、信用不安が高まっていることが鮮明となった。株価は一時、８．３％下落し、２０２５年５月以来の安値を付けた。

同社は約５００億ドルの債務を抱えており、データセンターブームが信用により支えられているという懸念の象徴となっている。また、新興企業の経営を圧迫しているほか、グーグルの持ち株会社アルファベットやメタ・プラットフォームズのような大手企業のキャッシュフローにまで圧力をかけている。

同社が４月に発行した２０３１年償還の社債の利回りは１６．２％となり、通常は財務悪化を示唆する水準を上回った。トレードウェブのデータによると、同社債の直近の価格は額面１ドルに対し０．０１１ドル安の０．７８４ドル。同社の債務に対するデフォルト保険コストは約１０００ベーシスポイント（ｂｐ）に上昇し、５年以内のデフォルト確率が約６３％であることを示唆する水準となった。１年前の同確率は約３０％だった。

同社の株価は１４日にも約１５％下落しており、ハイテク株売りの中でも下落幅の大きい銘柄の一つとなっている。

ＩＧグループのチーフテクニカルアナリスト、アクセル・ルドルフ氏は「ＡＩ需要と、収益性のあるビジネスモデルとは全く別物だということに市場は気付き始めている」と指摘。「現時点では、ＡＩコンピューティングへの需要が突然冷え込んだというよりは、投資家がインフラ拡充の資金調達方法を疑問視しているように見える。ただ、資本コストが上がり続ければ、需要が堅調であっても、過剰にレバレッジを掛けている企業を守るには十分でなくなる可能性がある」と述べた。

一方、同社の第２位の株主で約１０％の株式を保有する半導体大手エヌビディアのジェンスン・フアンＣＥＯは、こうした懸念を一蹴。ストックホルムでのイベントで記者団に対し「コアウィーブの財務力は日々改善している」とした上で、エヌビディアによる同社への支援は必要ないとの認識を示した。「私は楽観的だ。コアウィーブの資本コストは実際に下がっている」と語った。

ロイター 関連ニュース アングル：ＡＩ株売りに勢い、資金調達に懸念　クライマックスには距離 アングル：ＡＩ関連の資金調達、低格付け領域にも拡大　投資家は警戒感強める コラム：ベセント氏の危うい賭け、ＡＩ主導の経済成長は「債務病」の特効薬ならず コラム：ＩＴサービス企業、生成ＡＩ追い風に株価上昇か コラム：ＡＩ投資を「黄金」に変えたマイクロソフト、アルファベットは羨望か 最終更新: 10/16(金) 2:16 ロイター

item.title: Bones from Iraqi cave hint at violence and compassion in Neanderthals
item.description: Oct 15 : The bones of a Neanderthal from a cave in Iraq's Kurdistan region are offering evidence of both violence and compassion in the closest evolutionary cousins of our species, exhibiting a wound apparently from a fatal spear attack as well as signs of an earlier nonfatal injury that may have elicited kindly car

Bones from Iraqi cave hint at violence and compassion in Neanderthals

The entrance to Shanidar Cave in Iraq's Kurdistan region, a site of important Neanderthal remains, is seen in an undated photograph released on October 15, 2026. Prof Graeme Barker/Handout via REUTERS NO RESALES. NO ARCHIVES. THIS IMAGE HAS BEEN SUPPLIED BY A THIRD PARTY

FAST

Oct 15 : The bones of a Neanderthal from a cave in Iraq's Kurdistan region are offering evidence of both violence and compassion in the closest evolutionary cousins of our species, exhibiting a wound apparently from a fatal spear attack as well as signs of an earlier nonfatal injury that may have elicited kindly care. Researchers have discovered at Shanidar Cave in the Zagros Mountains of northern Iraq a partial skeleton of a Neanderthal, aged in the mid-40s, that included a left shoulder blade, or scapula, with a circular hole six-tenths of an inch (15 mm) wide indicative of a deeply penetrating stab. The bones of this individual, who they call Shanidar A, were unearthed from under about 25 feet (7.5 meters) of rocks and sediment inside the cave and date to about 75,000 years ago. The researchers were unable to determine Shanidar A's sex. The researchers said the injury's shape suggests it was caused by a forceful thrust using a sharpened wooden spear, a type of weapon Neanderthals are known to have used, rather than a spear with a stone tip. It was a weapon employed in hunting large mammals that were an important food source.
